title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act proposes legal measures to protect electoral integrity by regulating and limiting AI‑generated content that could mislead voters. It includes provisions to detect, label, and penalize deceptive AI output used in campaign materials and online platforms.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives states that Congress should not give extra money or special regulatory help to companies or banks that are in financial distress because of problems in the artificial‑intelligence market. Instead, Congress should focus on helping Americans who have been harmed by those AI‑related financial failures.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 establishes national standards to ensure AI systems are trustworthy, safe, and transparent. It requires researchers to disclose data sources, validate models, and follow ethical guidelines to prevent bias and misuse.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to publicly disclose the types of artificial‑intelligence systems it uses, how they influence decisions, and the data that feeds those systems. It also establishes regular audits, oversight procedures, and clear privacy safeguards to ensure veterans and the public understand and trust the VA’s AI practices.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act aims to ensure that artificial intelligence used in the Veterans Affairs claims process is transparent, fair, and accountable. It sets guidelines for how AI decisions should be documented, reviewed, and corrected to protect veterans' rights and prevent bias.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act establishes rules that require AI developers and businesses to disclose when content or services are powered by AI, ensuring consumers can easily recognize AI-generated information. It imposes penalties for misleading or deceptive AI practices, aiming to protect consumers from fraud and promote transparency and trust in AI-driven products and services.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act aims to strengthen the nation's AI infrastructure by establishing comprehensive security protocols and standards. It focuses on safeguarding AI systems against threats, ensuring resilience, and fostering collaboration among industry, academia, and government to build robust defense mechanisms.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act proposes creating a dedicated task force to enhance the security of AI systems. It aims to coordinate federal efforts in identifying, mitigating, and preventing AI-related cyber threats.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 establishes rules for identifying, assessing, and reducing risks in AI systems. It requires developers and users to implement strong security measures, conduct ongoing audits, and report incidents to protect public safety and maintain accountability.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 is a legislative proposal that aims to create a national framework for coordinating the development, deployment, and oversight of AI systems that directly interact with or control physical hardware. It seeks to ensure safety, accountability, and responsible innovation by promoting collaboration between government agencies, industry, and research institutions in managing the risks and benefits of AI-driven physical technologies.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act seeks to safeguard democratic processes by prohibiting the use of artificial intelligence that could mislead voters or influence election outcomes. It establishes legal frameworks to detect, regulate, and penalize AI-generated misinformation targeted at elections.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act is a proposed law that would require developers of AI systems capable of autonomous self‑enhancement to register their models and provide detailed documentation about their learning processes. It seeks to ensure transparency, safety, and accountability by establishing oversight mechanisms, reporting obligations, and enforcement procedures to protect public interests and prevent unintended harms.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act aims to suspend the development and operation of new AI data centers to address concerns about their environmental, societal, and regulatory impacts. It requires a comprehensive review and the establishment of guidelines before any new data center projects can resume.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act aims to curb the development and deployment of artificial intelligence that could act outside human control and pose significant risks to public safety and privacy. It establishes safeguards and oversight mechanisms to ensure AI technologies are transparent, accountable, and aligned with societal values.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board tasked with investigating cybersecurity incidents that involve artificial intelligence. The board will analyze threats, recommend policy changes, and help protect national security and public trust in AI technologies.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act proposes to shape AI development so that it directly benefits U.S. citizens, focusing on safety, transparency, and the creation of new jobs. It also calls for federal funding for AI research and public oversight to protect privacy, prevent discrimination, and ensure that AI systems are accountable to the people they serve.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires AI companies and research institutions in China to regularly submit detailed reports on their technologies and capabilities, helping the government monitor the sector’s growth and influence. It also establishes standards for data transparency, security compliance, and ethical practices to align AI development with national priorities and public safety.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 requires that all medical diagnosis, treatment, and patient care be performed by licensed physicians, not by artificial intelligence systems. It prohibits the use of AI as a primary provider of healthcare services and establishes strict penalties for entities that attempt to substitute AI for qualified doctors.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy proposes creating a new office within the Executive Office of the President to monitor and address risks from artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies. The office would coordinate national efforts to identify, assess, and mitigate threats posed by these advanced systems.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution creates a Select Committee focused on artificial intelligence. The committee will oversee AI developments, advise on policy, and promote responsible use of the technology.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a framework for assessing the potential risks associated with AI systems before they are deployed. It requires companies to conduct comprehensive risk evaluations and submit reports to a regulatory body, ensuring that safety and ethical considerations are prioritized.
